title: Tech News with G. Dai — Episode 8
intro: Namaste! Welcome to episode eight of Tech News with G. Dai. Five stories you need to know today. And the last one is a gaming laptop store now open in Kathmandu!

stories.headline: Anthropic: AI may soon build AI
stories.vo: This is huge for A-I! Anthropic says in a public filing that it may imminently reach the point where A-I speeds up its own development. It says no model has crossed that line yet.

stories.headline: Nepal's e-GP tender system is back
stories.vo: Good news for Nepal contractors! The upgraded e-G-P system is live again after being suspended in August over security risks. It now has two-factor login and encrypted bids. Contract management comes in phase two.

stories.headline: Google backs down on school Search plan
stories.vo: Here's a surprise! Google planned to switch off Search for schools that refused its A-I tools. After loud backlash, it now says Gemini and Search will be off by default, and schools can choose.

stories.headline: Apple: dating apps must be 18+
stories.vo: Parents, take note! Apple now says any app with dating features must be rated eighteen plus, and A-I companion apps with romantic content get tighter limits for minors. New rules start November sixteenth.

stories.headline: ASUS opens first own store in Nepal
stories.vo: Gamers, this one is for you! A-S-U-S opened its first own-brand store in Putalisadak, Kathmandu. You can try R-O-G laptops with R-T-X fifty ninety graphics before you buy.

outro: That's your tech brief for today. Should schools be forced to use A-I? Tell me in the comments, and follow G. Robotics so you never miss tomorrow's brief.
caption:
Anthropic says AI may soon help build its own next version. Should we worry? 🤖

1️⃣ 🤖 Anthropic: AI may soon build AI
2️⃣ 🇳🇵 Nepal's e-GP tender system is back
3️⃣ 🏫 Google backs down on school Search plan
4️⃣ 📱 Apple: dating apps must be 18+
5️⃣ 💻 ASUS opens first own store in Nepal

Should schools be forced to use AI? Tell us in the comments!

G. Dai is an AI-generated presenter.
Sources: TechCrunch, NepaliTelecom
